messages:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a 12% tail latency bump on host-side when we flipped the new kernel-prefetch heuristic yesterday evening. Correlation looks strongest with short streaming requests (<=128 tokens) over gRPC.
Maria: Ugh. I noticed more CPU time in the parse/serialize path in the flamegraphs, did you get a pprof? :thinking_face:
Alex: Uploaded a quick heap/CPU sample to the perf collector: https://perf.internal/runs/1777771001 — flame shows a new hotpath in TokenConverter::normalize (host-preproc).
Jamal: Can you paste the hot stack? wondering if it's our new UTF-8 normalization or the multi-fragment coalesce.
Alex: Stack snippet: `TokenConverter::normalize -> RequestParser::feed -> StreamFramer::emit_chunk -> GrpcWritev::flush` — lots of small writes showing up.
Maria: That stack points to extra allocations during normalize, likely due to the new kernel selection code returning variable-size id maps. I have a repro locally with a synthetic 64-token stream.
Lina: Might be the repeated KV-cache lookups we added for kernel hints. If each token triggers a map lookup + small alloc we can easily blow up short-request overhead.
Jamal: Agreed. Two quick checks: 1) counters for kv_hit vs kv_miss per request, 2) number of allocations per request (malloc count).
perf-bot: Perf-run 1777771001 summary: mean latency +9.8%, p95 +12.1%, CPU sys +6.5%. Artifact: https://perf.internal/artifacts/1777771001.tar.gz
Maria: I ran `malloc_stats` on the repro — allocations/request jumped from ~18 to ~73 after the change. Biggest culprit: transient string copies in normalize.
Alex: Reproduced locally. Patch idea: make normalize operate in-place with an arena buffer and avoid per-token std::string creation. Also short-circuit kernel hint path for requests < 96 tokens.
Jamal: Short-circuit sounds safe as a canary. Can we gate it behind a runtime flag so we can A/B?
Lina: Yes, add `--ingress-mini-kt-skip` flag default true for canary off. We should also add a metric `ingress-mini-allocs` to monitor.
Maria: I prototyped an arena approach — `ArenaBuffer::reserve(n)` then write token bytes directly, reduces allocations by ~60% on the repro. Patch WIP: `ingress/host/token_conv_arena.{cc,h}`
Alex: Nice. Another angle: coalesce small gRPC writes in the proxy layer so we do fewer writev syscalls. There's a small window in GrpcWritev::flush that emits many writes per token.
Jamal: Coalescing is additive; even with arena we still benefit. Let's do both: arena + writev coalesce. Plan: (1) revert kernel-prefetch heuristic rollout to 25% traffic, (2) enable arena on all hosts behind a feature flag, (3) enable writev coalesce in edge proxy.
Lina: I'll open the rollback/feature-flag PRs and add the metrics dashboard entries. Can we add alerting if p95 rises >6% in the next hour?
Alex: Please do. Also add a short-term tracing tag `host:kernel-prefetch` on requests so we can filter perf traces.
Maria: One more datapoint — KV cache hit rate decreased by ~7% after the change (likely more probing on startup). If we can reduce redundant lookups by caching per-request kernel hint we should see improvement.
Jamal: Good call. Cache per-request kernel hint in ThreadLocalRequestState and avoid re-lookup on subsequent tokens.
perf-bot: Scheduled perf re-run after canary rollback at 1777771100.
Alex: Ok proceeding with the rollback and arena patch. Will post PR numbers here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
